Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

quality noun

a characteristic, a trait

also characteristic, trait, attribute, good qualities

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.56: singulārum rērum singulās proprietātēs esse

proprietās, proprietātis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a property, a quality peculiar to a thing

Other words

  • virtūs, virtūtis f. — a good quality, an excellence; in the plural, someone’s good qualities

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 23: virtūtēs continentiae, gravitātis, jūstitiae, fideī (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • proprium, propriī n. — what is characteristic of someone or something

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 42.4: proprium hūmānī ingeniī est ōdisse quem laeserīs · Declension on Wiktionary

    proprium est + genitive, it is characteristic of.

  • quālitās, quālitātis f. — a quality, a property (in philosophy)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 1.25 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Cicero coined it for Greek ποιότης, a philosophers’ word even in Greek, as he says; frequent only in later prose (Lewis & Short). It does not by itself mean good quality.

Examples

  • singulārum rērum singulās proprietātēs esse

    that each single thing has its own particular qualitiesCic. Ac. 2.56

  • quālitātēs igitur appellāvī quās ποιότητας Graecī vocant, quod ipsum apud Graecōs nōn est vulgī verbum sed philosophōrum

    so I have called “qualities” what the Greeks call poiotētes; and even among the Greeks that is not a word of ordinary people but of philosophersCic. Ac. 1.25

See also quality, nature, kind.
